headline: A critical LMCache flaw lets someone run code remotely without logging in, and no fix exists yet.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: new disclosure on 7 Oct, read in full; never raised.
importance_line: What changed: a critical flaw with no fix is public, which affects operators who run LMCache on a reachable address and the companies using those AI servers; the doubt is that LMCache has published no advisory, and the six extra reports from one account are unconfirmed.
summary: The Hacker News reports that JFrog disclosed on 7 October a flaw, CVE-2026-105192, that lets an attacker who can reach an LMCache server run commands without logging in, rated 9.8 out of 10 for a server bound to a routable address. It matters because LMCache speeds up large AI language model servers such as vLLM, and with no patched release JFrog advises keeping the port on a local or trusted network.
notes: Full article read. Single firm's disclosure; LMCache has not published an advisory.
